# Avoid relying on untrusted data for server-side selection

## What This Skill Does
This skill fixes cases where C++ code uses request, CLI, or other untrusted input to choose a server-side page, view, template, file, include target, or loop/allocation size. The safe pattern is to validate input early with a strict token rule, map accepted values to a fixed internal enum-like selection, reject unknown values, and bound any numeric input before it affects iteration or memory use.

## Decision Table
| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Raw user input is passed to template, file, page, or view selection code | Apply this fix |
| Input is used with `std::ifstream`, template loaders, include targets, or routing selectors | Replace raw string selection with an allowlist resolver that returns an internal enum or fixed identifier |
| Text selection input is expected | Validate with a strict alphanumeric whitelist, reject empty or oversized values, then check membership in a known set |
| The same untrusted input also controls counts, indexes, loops, or allocation sizes | Parse to a numeric type and enforce explicit min/max bounds before use |
| Code already maps validated input to fixed internal selections and rejects unknown values | No action needed |

## Boundaries

### Can Do
- Replace raw selector strings with fixed allowlist resolution and enum-like internal IDs
- Add strict validation for selection tokens such as alphanumeric-only and length limits
- Add bounded numeric parsing when untrusted input also drives loops, pagination, or allocation

### Cannot Do
- Infer the correct business allowlist values without project context
- Guarantee template engines or routing frameworks are safe if they still accept dynamic raw names elsewhere
- Fix unrelated file access, authorization, or path traversal issues beyond the selection flow being changed

## Gotchas
- Validating format without checking allowed values: alphanumeric input like `admin` or `unknown` can still select unintended code paths if membership is not enforced
- Checking the allowlist but continuing to use the original string: this defeats the fix; use only the mapped internal enum or fixed identifier afterward
- Bounding counts but not rejecting overflow or parse failures: very large numeric strings can still cause exceptions, wraparound, or excessive allocation if parsing is not strict

## Quick Verification
```bash
# Confirm a secure resolver/validator exists
rg -n --glob '*.{c,cc,cpp,cxx,h,hpp,hxx}' '(resolve_template_id|select_page|validate_selection|is_strict_token|is_alphanumeric_only|parse_bounded_count|enum class (TemplateId|Page))'

# Find likely unguarded dangerous server-side selection/file-loading calls fed by variables
rg -n --glob '*.{c,cc,cpp,cxx,h,hpp,hxx}' '(std::ifstream\s+\w+\s*\(\s*\w+\s*\)|loadTemplate\s*\(\s*\w+\s*\)|renderPage\s*\(\s*\w+\s*\)|fopen\s*\(\s*\w+\s*,|open\s*\(\s*\w+\s*,)'

# Build and test with the detected C++ toolchain/project shape
if [ -f CMakeLists.txt ]; then cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure; elif [ -f Makefile ]; then make && make test; else find . -type f \( -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.cc' -o -name '*.cxx' \) -print0 | xargs -0 -r g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -O2 -o /tmp/verify-cpp-build && /tmp/verify-cpp-build; fi
```

# Avoid relying on untrusted data for server-side selection

## What This Skill Does
This skill fixes CWE-673 style server-side selection flaws in C code where untrusted input is used to pick a page, template, include, or file for rendering or processing. It replaces direct use of user-controlled selectors in APIs such as `fopen()` with one shared resolver that enforces a maximum length, full-string allowlist-style format validation, exact membership in a fixed approved set, and fail-closed behavior for missing or unknown values.

## Decision Table
| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Request data, argv, env, headers, or form input is passed directly or indirectly to `fopen()`, template loading, or server-side rendering selection | Apply this fix |
| Template or page names are built by concatenating, formatting, or transforming untrusted input | Replace with a static allowlist resolver that maps approved selector keys to fixed paths |
| Selector validation checks only for "bad" characters or does partial matching | Replace with full-string positive validation plus exact allowlist membership checks |
| Selector accepts arbitrary-length alphanumeric input | Add a strict maximum length check before format validation or lookup |
| Code already resolves selectors only through a shared static allowlist and rejects invalid input | No action needed |

## Boundaries

### Can Do
- Add a shared resolver such as `resolve_allowed_template()` that maps approved selector names to fixed server-owned paths
- Add strict selector validation using length checks, `isalnum()`, and exact `strcmp()` membership checks
- Refactor direct `fopen(selector, ...)` style selection to use a resolved path returned by the allowlist

### Cannot Do
- Prove that every possible server-side renderer or include mechanism in the whole program is safe without code review of all call paths
- Safely preserve behavior that depends on free-form user-selected template or file names
- Fix separate issues such as unsafe SSI execution, command injection via `system()`, or unsafe template engine features unless they are also explicitly changed

## Gotchas
- Validating format but not membership: alphanumeric-only input like `admin` or `debug` can still select unintended resources if you do not enforce an exact approved set
- Falling back to user-derived defaults: rejecting bad input is required; do not strip characters and continue, and do not derive fallback file names from the rejected selector
- Duplicating validation at call sites: inconsistent checks lead to bypasses; route every selector through one shared resolver before any `fopen()` or similar server-side selection call

## Quick Verification
```bash
# Confirm the secure resolver/validation functions exist
rg -n 'resolve_allowed_template|validate_template_name_length|validate_template_name_format|validate_template_name_allowed|ALLOWED_TEMPLATES' .

# Find unguarded dangerous file-selection calls that may still use untrusted input directly
rg -n 'fopen\s*\([^,)]*(argv\[|getenv\s*\(|scanf\s*\(|fgets\s*\(|recv\s*\(|read\s*\(|user_selected_template|selector|template|path)' .

# Build all C files generically with warnings enabled
find . -type f \( -name '*.c' -o -name '*.h' \) >/dev/null && cc -Wall -Wextra -Werror -std=c11 $(find . -type f -name '*.c') -o /tmp/skill-check-bin

# Run available project tests if present; otherwise at least execute the built binary if creation succeeded
[ -f Makefile ] && make test || [ -f CMakeLists.txt ] && cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure || [ -x /tmp/skill-check-bin ] && /tmp/skill-check-bin home
```

# Avoid Untrusted Data for Server-Side Selection

## What This Skill Does
This skill fixes cases where untrusted input is used to choose a server-side page, view, template, include target, or file. In JavaScript, this often appears as request data or CLI arguments being concatenated into template names, file paths, or `res.render()` selectors. The fix is to validate type, enforce a strict whitelist and small maximum length, then resolve input only through a server-controlled immutable allowlist of permitted resources, rejecting unknown values without fallback.

## Decision Table
| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Request data, route params, query params, body fields, headers, env vars, or CLI args are concatenated into template names, file names, include paths, or `res.render()` values | Apply this fix |
| Code uses `fs.readFileSync`, `fs.readFile`, `path.join`, `path.resolve`, or `res.render` with user-controlled selectors | Replace direct selection with a frozen mapping or explicit allowed set |
| Selector is intended to choose one of a small known set such as `home`, `about`, or `profile` | Add type check, strict whitelist regex, max length check, and allowed-set membership check |
| Code already uses a server-controlled immutable mapping and rejects unknown, non-whitelisted, or oversized values | No action needed |
| Code falls back to a default page when validation fails | Reject the input instead of silently selecting a resource |

## Boundaries

### Can Do
- Replace direct server-side resource selection with a fixed server-controlled mapping
- Add strict selector validation for type, format, length, and allowed values
- Find common JavaScript danger patterns involving `fs`, `path`, and template rendering APIs

### Cannot Do
- Guarantee safety if other code later uses the validated value to build new paths or dynamic includes
- Infer the correct business allowlist without project knowledge of valid pages or templates
- Fix client-side template injection or unrelated file access issues outside the selection flow

## Gotchas
- Validating with a loose regex only: this is wrong because `admin` may match the format but still be an unapproved selector unless checked against an explicit allowed set
- Falling back to `home` on invalid input: this is wrong because it hides attacks and still performs server-side selection instead of rejecting unsafe input
- Using `path.join(viewsDir, userInput + '.html')` after validation alone: this is wrong because selection should come from a server-defined mapping, not directly from user data

## Quick Verification
```bash
# Confirm a guard or allowlist exists
rg -n "Object\.freeze|new Set\(|ALLOWED_[A-Z_]+|TEMPLATE_MAP|PAGE_NAME_PATTERN|isAllowed[A-Z]\w+" .

# Find likely unguarded dangerous server-side selection patterns
rg -n "res\.render\s*\(\s*(req|request|ctx|argv|process\.argv)|fs\.(readFileSync|readFile)\s*\(\s*path\.(join|resolve)\([^)]*(req|request|ctx|argv|process\.argv)|path\.(join|resolve)\([^)]*(req\.|request\.|ctx\.|argv|process\.argv)" .

# Build + test using whichever JavaScript toolchain the project provides
npm test || yarn test || pnpm test || bun test
```

# Avoid relying on untrusted data for server-side selection

## What This Skill Does
This skill fixes cases where untrusted input controls which server-side page, view, template, or file-backed template resource gets selected. In Python, the safe pattern is to treat user input only as a lookup key into a fixed server-defined mapping, validate it with a strict full-input allowlist, enforce membership in an approved set, and fail closed for unknown values instead of concatenating input into template names, file paths, include targets, or `open()` calls.

## Decision Table
| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| User input is passed to `open()`, template loaders, or path-building code to choose a page/template | Replace direct selection with a fixed server-side mapping such as `TEMPLATES[validated_key]` |
| A selector comes from request params, route params, CLI args, env vars, or job payloads | Validate type, length, and full-input allowlist before any selection logic |
| Selector format is valid but value is not one of the known server-defined choices | Reject with a safe error or use a fixed safe default chosen by server code |
| Code uses Flask/Jinja rendering such as `render_template_string()` after reading a file chosen by input | Remove the file selection path and select only from approved in-memory or server-defined templates |
| Code already validates with `fullmatch()` and checks membership in a fixed set/map before selection | No action needed |

## Boundaries

### Can Do
- Replace untrusted selector-driven resource selection with a fixed mapping
- Add strict selector validation using `re.fullmatch()` plus length/type checks
- Add explicit membership checks against a server-defined allowed set

### Cannot Do
- Prove a selector is safe if it still directly controls file paths, template names, or include targets
- Infer the correct business-approved selector list without project knowledge
- Fix unrelated template injection, XSS, or authorization flaws beyond selector handling

## Gotchas
- Using regex validation alone: syntactically valid but unknown values can still select unintended resources unless membership is checked too
- Using `re.match()` instead of `fullmatch()`: partial matches can allow dangerous trailing content such as traversal or markup
- Falling back to `open(page_name)` or dynamic template names on validation failure: this reintroduces untrusted server-side selection instead of failing closed

## Quick Verification
```bash
# Confirm a strict validator or approved mapping exists
rg -n "fullmatch\(|re\.compile\(|ALLOWED_SELECTORS|TEMPLATES\s*=\s*\{|validate_page_name\(" .

# Find unguarded dangerous file/template selection patterns driven by input
rg -n "open\s*\(|render_template\s*\(|render_template_string\s*\(" . 

# Build + test using common Python entry points across app types
python -m compileall . && (python -m pytest -q || python -m unittest discover -v)
```

# Avoid relying on untrusted data for server-side selection

## What This Skill Does
This skill fixes cases where Node.js code lets untrusted input control which server-side page, view, template, or include file gets selected or processed. The safe pattern is to treat external input only as a small validated key, enforce strict type/length/character checks, compare it against a fixed allowlist, and map it to internal identifiers instead of concatenating raw input into file paths, template names, `res.render(...)` arguments, or SSI/include targets.

## Decision Table
| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Request params, query, body, headers, cookies, CLI args, or stored user settings are used to build a template name, page name, or file path | Apply this fix |
| Code concatenates input into `path.join(...)`, `fs.readFileSync(...)`, `require(...)`, or `res.render(...)` for server-side selection | Replace raw selection with strict validation plus a fixed allowlist mapping |
| A template/include key is already validated for type, max length, character set, and membership in an explicit allowlist | No action needed |
| Well-formed but unknown values such as `admin` or `contact` are currently accepted | Reject them unless they exist in the server-side mapping |
| SSI-style include directives are processed from selected files | Restrict include targets to a separate fixed allowlist or remove dynamic include handling |

## Boundaries

### Can Do
- Replace raw page or template selection with allowlist-backed lookup functions
- Add strict validation for selection keys using built-in checks or Ajv schemas
- Flag unguarded Node.js sinks such as `fs.readFileSync`, `path.join`, and `res.render` when they use untrusted input

### Cannot Do
- Prove whether every upstream input source is trusted without reviewing calling code
- Secure arbitrary template engines or custom SSI processors beyond enforcing fixed allowed targets
- Prevent issues in files that are already unsafe internally if the selected file itself contains dangerous logic

## Gotchas
- Allowing regex-only validation without an allowlist: a value like `admin` can match the pattern and still select unintended content
- Using `path.normalize()` or `path.join()` as the main defense: these APIs build paths; they do not make attacker-controlled selection safe
- Mapping keys directly to user-influenced filenames: the mapping must return fixed internal identifiers, not partially concatenated input

```bash
# Confirm a secure allowlist/mapping or guard exists
rg -n "ALLOWED_[A-Z_]+|TEMPLATE_MAP|PAGE_NAME_PATTERN|isAllowedPageName|validateTemplateSelection|hasOwnProperty\.call\(" .
```

# Avoid relying on untrusted data for server-side selection

## What This Skill Does
This skill fixes cases where C# code lets request data, command input, or other untrusted values decide which server-side page, view, template, include, or file gets resolved. The safe pattern is to normalize input, validate it as a short symbolic selector, enforce exact membership in a finite allowlist, and return only server-defined targets from a fixed mapping. If legacy file-backed templates remain, canonicalize the mapped path and verify it stays under a trusted root. Never concatenate raw input into template names, view names, include directives, or file paths.

## Decision Table
| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| User input is concatenated into `Path.Combine(...)`, `File.ReadAllText(...)`, view/template names, or `".tpl"`/`".cshtml"` suffixes | Apply a selector-to-target mapping and stop using raw input for server-side selection |
| Code accepts a page/view/template selector from HTTP, CLI, config, queue, or deserialized input | Normalize, length-check, regex-validate, and enforce exact allowlist membership before resolution |
| Legacy code still resolves file-backed templates after mapping | Canonicalize with `Path.GetFullPath` and ensure the resolved file stays under one trusted root |
| User input can reach dynamic rendering, include, or template execution flows | Reject unknown selectors and pass only constant server-defined targets into rendering/include APIs |
| Code already uses exact allowlisted mapping with constant targets and optional trusted-root path check | No action needed |

## Boundaries

### Can Do
- Replace raw page/view/template/file selection with a fixed `Dictionary` or `HashSet` allowlist
- Add strict selector validation using `Trim`, length checks, `Regex`, and `StringComparer.Ordinal`
- Add canonical path enforcement with `Path.GetFullPath` for legacy file-backed templates

### Cannot Do
- Prove every downstream template engine is safe if it interprets file contents as executable server-side syntax
- Infer the correct business allowlist of selectors without application knowledge
- Fix unrelated output encoding or content injection issues inside the selected template

## Gotchas
- Trimming without allowlist mapping: trimmed input like `Home` may still be dangerous if raw input is later concatenated into a path or view name
- Using case-insensitive matching by default: `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase` can allow near matches that resolve to unintended targets; prefer exact deterministic matching unless the app explicitly requires otherwise
- Checking path traversal before mapping: validating attacker input directly is weaker than mapping first to trusted internal relative paths, then canonicalizing the resolved path

## Quick Verification
```bash
# Confirm secure selector guards/mappings exist
rg -n 'TryGetValue\(|Contains\(|StringComparer\.Ordinal|Path\.GetFullPath\(|Regex\("^\[A-Za-z0-9\]\{1,32\}\$"' .

# Find likely unguarded dangerous server-side selection/file resolution calls
rg -n 'Path\.Combine\(|File\.ReadAllText\(|File\.OpenRead\(|FileStream\(|Directory\.GetFiles\(|return\s+View\(|PartialView\(|View\(\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\)|new\s+Regex\(' . \
  -g '!bin' -g '!obj'

# Build and run tests across common C# project layouts
dotnet build
dotnet test
```

## What This Skill Does
This skill fixes cases where untrusted input influences which server-side page, template, fragment, include target, or view gets resolved in Java code. The safe pattern is to treat user input only as a logical selector, validate it with strict anchored allowlist and length checks, require membership in a closed approved set, and resolve it through a fixed server-side mapping that fails closed for unknown values.

## Decision Table
| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| User input is concatenated into a JSP path, template name, fragment path, SSI directive, or include target | Replace direct construction with a server-side `Map` from logical keys to constant internal resources |
| Code accepts selectors such as `page`, `view`, `template`, `fragment`, or `section` from request, CLI, message, or job input | Add strict validation with `Pattern.compile("^[A-Za-z0-9]+$")` and explicit min/max length checks before lookup |
| Input is syntactically valid but may name internal or debug-only resources | Enforce membership with an immutable `Set.of(...)` approved selector list and reject unknown values |
| Unknown selector currently falls back to user-derived resolution | Fail closed with a safe error result or exception; do not attempt fallback resolution from input |
| Code already uses constant internal paths resolved only from validated approved keys | No action needed |

## Boundaries

### Can Do
- Replace user-controlled server-side resource selection with fixed `Map`-based resolution
- Add Java validation using `java.util.regex.Pattern` and explicit length checks
- Add immutable membership checks with `Set.of(...)` and closed failure behavior

### Cannot Do
- Prove every framework-specific render path is safe without reviewing all call sites
- Infer the correct approved selector list or internal view mapping without application context
- Fix client-side routing or browser-side template selection issues unrelated to server-side resolution

## Gotchas
- Validation without membership checks: alphanumeric values like `debug` or `admin` may still reach unintended resources if they are not rejected by an approved set
- Partial or unanchored regex checks: patterns that do not enforce full-string matches can let dangerous input through after substring matches
- Safe validator but unsafe fallback: even validated code is still vulnerable if unknown selectors trigger string concatenation, `getOrDefault(...)`, or dynamic include/render behavior from user input
